short: An unprepared king whose reign covered the war, Indian independence and austerity.
full:
Albert, Duke of York, became king on his brother's abdication and took the name George VI to signal continuity with his father. Shy and afflicted with a stammer he worked on for years with the therapist Lionel Logue, he was widely thought unsuited to the role, and did much to restore confidence in the institution after the crisis of 1936.

He and Queen Elizabeth stayed in London through the Blitz, and Buckingham Palace was bombed several times. His broadcasts and his visits to bombed cities, factories and troops made the monarchy a fixture of the home front. After the war he presided over the Attlee government's welfare state and nationalisations, and over the beginning of the end of the empire he had inherited: India and Pakistan became independent in 1947, and he dropped the title Emperor of India the following year. Heavy smoking wrecked his health, and he died at Sandringham in February 1952, aged 56.
